work.objective: Review rkendel1/appboundry for an unresolved reliability defect in packages/appboundry-host (the artifact host: guest execution and limits, collections and transactions, identity and sessions, backups, the capability ledger). The after-commit outbox (performOutbox, recoverOutbox, retryOutbox) is already tracked in issue #99; look elsewhere. Find one defect you can prove with a failing test.

findings.title: tenancy@1 commit reports any FeltDB failure, including an unconfirmed commit, as a CONFLICT where 'nothing was written'
findings.summary: TenancyTransaction.commit() catches every error from db.transaction() and rethrows it as HostError CONFLICT with the message 'nothing was written'. It does not look at the error. When FeltDB answers COMMIT_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN or DURABILITY_FAILURE, the transaction may already have been applied. ArtifactHost.tenancy() awaits tx.commit() (host.ts:463), so the caller is told the membership or tenant change did not happen and that retrying is safe. A retried provision mints a fresh crypto.token tenant id and creates a second organization or membership. The collections path maps the same FeltDB codes to OUTCOME_UNKNOWN (collections.ts commitError, lines 191-196); the tenancy path does not. The new test simulates an authority that applies the write and then loses the acknowledgement: the write lands, yet commit() rejects with code CONFLICT and 'nothing was written'.

findings.fix: In TenancyTransaction.commit(), map FeltDB errors as commitError does. Only PRECONDITION_FAILED becomes CONFLICT ('nothing was written'). COMMIT_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and DURABILITY_FAILURE become OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, with a hint to read before retrying. Contract violations and refusals keep their own codes, for example via feltdbRefusal/feltdbFailure. Also pass a stable transactionId so FeltDB can deduplicate a resend.
